scope: Single-sheet schematics generated from a pinned intended circuit. Keep component references, values, and electrical connectivity unchanged while improving presentation.
source_documents: Owner direction 2026-10-27: accept power symbols for rails, as conventional 555 schematics draw them

Owner direction 2026-11-12: add measured readability gates for defects the v3 checks and model review missed (review_qualification_v3_2026-11-12_qwen35_256k_run1); rail detours use a ratio with a minimum detour
Owner direction 2026-11-12: centre the drawing on the page and gate page balance; the 65% utilization target never failed and is removed
Owner direction 2026-11-12: gate reference/value text that reads as another part's (historical R1/R2 text, led_series detached value)

criteria.requirement: Every required component reference and value is legible and clearly associated with its own symbol.

measurements.source: schematic review engine default maximum field-envelope distance
independent native symbol-anchor and text-envelope observer

measurements.unit: visible reference/value fields more than 5.08 mm from their own unit's drawing and nearer another part's drawing (units drawn without a body exempt)
measurements.source: independent native text-envelope and symbol body/pin-stub geometry

visual_rubric: Read each reference and value on the full-page image or its supplied detail image; flag fields that are too small, clipped, visually stranded, or ambiguous despite passing distance checks.
Confirm each field is visually closest and clearly related to its owning symbol, not a neighboring symbol.
criteria.limitation: The 25.4 mm locality limit and non-overlap checks catch specific geometric defects; they do not establish human legibility or association by themselves. The 5.08 mm owner-advantage heuristic catches gross geometric mismatches; it does not prove human association. The nearest-owner gate measures gaps to drawn bodies and pin stubs, not to wires: text stranded above an unrelated wire, or far from every part, can still pass. Labels of units drawn without a body are not measured.

criteria.requirement: The page has balanced functional grouping, clear reading flow, and enough space to follow the circuit without crowding.

measurements.unit: wires crossing, or running along, the pin-name column of a unit drawn without a body
measurements.source: independent native wire and bodyless-unit pin-column geometry

measurements.unit: offset of the drawing's centre (wires, symbol bodies and visible text) from the usable frame centre, as a fraction of the frame's half-width and half-height; the drawing must also lie inside the frame and clear of the title block
measurements.source: independent native drawing extent against the usable A4 frame

visual_rubric: Inspect the full page for recognizable functional groups and a natural signal-flow direction.
Flag excessive unused space, crowding, fragmented motifs, confusing crossings, or a page that requires zooming to understand the main organization.
Use the detail image to confirm that local labels, pins, wires, and branches remain easy to follow.
criteria.limitation: Balance is measured as the centre of the drawing's bounding box; it does not judge grouping, reading flow or crowding inside the drawing, which remain visual judgments. Small circuits still use little of an A4 sheet; no minimum fill is set. The bodyless-unit clearance gate only covers wires through a power unit's pin-name column.

criteria.requirement: Every terminal of an asserted REF/VCC rail is visibly connected to that rail: either by continuous wires to a shared rail, or by a matching power symbol (ground glyph for return rails, supply arrow otherwise) on each separately drawn terminal group. Repeated same-name net labels alone are not accepted.

measurements.source: independent native netlist comparison to the pinned intended circuit
independent native wire-geometry grouping of asserted-net terminals; each separated group must touch a power symbol whose value names that rail

measurements.unit: power-symbol glyph or value boxes touching another symbol, field, label, visible pin number or foreign wire
measurements.source: native power-symbol geometry from the locked KiCad 10.0.6 power library

measurements.unit: ratio of a rail wire group's length to the rectilinear spanning tree of the terminals and power symbols it joins; only detours longer than 7.62 mm count
measurements.source: independent native wire grouping against the observed terminal inventory

measurements.unit: supply arrows pointing down or ground glyphs pointing up on the page
measurements.source: native power-symbol orientation from the locked KiCad 10.0.6 power library

visual_rubric: For each REF or VCC net in the intended circuit, confirm that every terminal either joins a visible common wire trunk or ends at a clearly drawn power symbol naming that rail; flag terminals connected only by text labels.
Check that power symbols read naturally (ground glyphs below or beside their terminals, supply arrows above or beside them), do not crowd nearby parts or text, and that names are legible.
Check that branch junctions are visibly unambiguous and do not visually merge distinct supply or return nets.
criteria.limitation: Netlist equivalence proves electrical identity. The rail-presentation gate proves that every separated rail group is joined by wire or marked by a matching power symbol; power-symbol clearance uses conservative glyph and text boxes. Neither proves human readability, and the visual rubric is not yet qualified. Power symbols are global connections: the KiCad netlist, not the drawing, establishes that they join the intended terminals. The rail-route detour gate measures rail wiring only, not signal nets; sideways power symbols are allowed.
